findings.summary: wf_evidence_put/wf_evidence_migrate write payloads to '.katana/runtime/evidence/<folder_id>/<filename>', but that directory is never registered as an allowed ignored runtime-state path. GovernedKernel._runtime_state_allowances (mcp/kernel/katana_kernel/kernel.py:154-170) returns only the manifests dir plus the mutation-ledger files, and require_clean_working_tree (mcp/kernel/katana_kernel/gitops.py:517-539) fails closed with DirtyWorkTreeError on any ignored untracked path outside those allowances whenever scope_prefixes is empty. server.configure() calls kernel.reconcile("work-folder") with no scope (mcp/work-folder/katana_work_folder_mcp/server.py:421), so after the very first evidence artifact lands in runtime the work-folder MCP service can no longer start — which also breaks the spec §4 'systemctl --user restart katana-work-folder-mcp' rollback drill. The same unscoped guard is used by GovernedKernel._reconcile_pending (kernel.py:420-426, 452-457), so crash recovery would mark otherwise-recoverable mutations BROKEN once evidence exists. The new tests never call configure()/reconcile, so the regression suite cannot catch it.

The folder reference file is content-addressed as 'evidence/<sha256>.sha256' while the runtime original is name-addressed as '.katana/runtime/evidence/<folder_id>/<filename>'. Re-putting the same filename with new content overwrites the runtime original but writes an additional new reference file and never removes the previous one, leaving committed stale pointers whose sha256 can no longer be recomputed from any runtime artifact. That breaks the frozen acceptance command §5.3 ('folder 内引用文件可 sha256sum 复算出 runtime 产物 hash') and lets pointer files accumulate on exactly the high-frequency rewrite path the spec targets. No test covers a same-filename re-put with changed content.

Spec §6 minimum delivery item 4 ('三服务回滚预案随附') is not delivered: the implementation commit touches only fs_tools.py, server.py, store.py and two test modules, and no rollback/runbook document for the katana-{work-folder,memory,wiki}-mcp restart procedure was added anywhere under docs/.

The runtime payload is written with a direct Path.write_bytes before the governed VFS reference write inside the same mutation callback, so a policy rejection or failed commit after that point leaves an orphan runtime file (and, for migrate, a runtime copy alongside the still-committed original). The direction is fail-safe, but the orphan is never journaled or cleaned up.
